One value: this was a yes, and I rewrote it. With LOOKAHEAD 1 s and a 16000-sample window, limit = LOOKAHEAD\u00b7SR + window = 32000 equalled the wrong form 2\u00b7LOOKAHEAD\u00b7SR. I changed the window to 8000 samples: limit 24000 samples / 48000 bytes, release to 8000, settled absolute count 32000. Now neither 2\u00b7LOOKAHEAD\u00b7SR (32000) nor LOOKAHEAD\u00b7SR (16000) matches. C1 reads the duration at two values (absent, and 7754 s far over every old cap) and on two paths (JSON and stored). The removed size cap is read with a declared size over both the old 1 GiB and the rig's max_bytes.\n\n5. The double: this was a yes, and I rewrote it. The C2 test replaced `worker.stream_media`, which this project owns (data/source_fetch.py), with a no-op. It now runs the real stream_media against the rig's ScriptedHost behind `data.source_fetch.build_opener`, which is the remote network and a severed layer. The fake ffmpeg is now a pass-through: stdin is copied to stdout in one write. I added a control at :159 (media.opened == [MEDIA_URL]) and the in-order byte check at :162. The remaining doubles are all severed layers: StubRunner for the GPU Whisper model (the existing rig's pattern), the scripted hosts for the network, and FFMPEG_ARGS for the external ffmpeg binary.\n\n6. It collects: yes. Every imported name exists in tests/active/test_translate_worker.py: MEDIA_HOST, MEDIA_URL, ScriptedHost, StubRunner, VIDEO_URL, _dispatching_opener, _worker, clip, rig. The run printed \"collected 5 items\": 4 parametrized C1 cases plus 1 C2 test, as written. The `--collect-only` summary printing \"no tests\" is that wrapper's summary format; the real run collects 5.\n\n7. Observed, not predicted: partly yes. I ran a probe (tests/tmp/probe_56_phase1_pipe.py, now emptied) that put the plan's reference AudioPipe (plan 57-56 lines 1374\u20131440: limit, base, clamped read, release, absolute wait_samples/slice) onto a fresh worker module, with the real stream_media given a large max_bytes. It ran this test body against that and five wrong variants. The reference PASSED. The variants failed as follows:\n- unclamped at :130 with `65536 <= 48000`\n- no-park at :130 with `256000 <= 48000`\n- silent-release at :140 with `(24000, 24000)`\n- relative-count at :140 with `(24000, 24000)`\n- dropping-release at :161 with `127999 == 128000`\n\nSo every C2 expected value was seen. For C1, CLIP_CUES and ready/whisper come from an earlier probe of an in-cap JSON-4 s run on this rig. The capped refusals were seen in this run. The ready outcome for the uncapped inputs cannot be observed until the phase exists: running these four cases after implementation is what confirms it.\n\n8. Red, not green: yes, it fails. ValidateTests: `5 failed`, `[exit status 1]`.\n\n9. Red for the right reason: yes.\n- C1: all four cases fail at :80, the assertion that judges the code, on the old caps' refusals: `assert ('failed', 'w...tion unknown') == ('ready', 'whisper', None)`, `('failed', 'w...754s over 5s')` twice (JSON and stored), and `('failed', 'w...128078 bytes')` (the media-size precheck against max_bytes).\n- C2: fails at :124 with `AttributeError: <module 'translate_worker' ...> has no attribute 'LOOKAHEAD_SECONDS'`. That is the phase's own new constant (plan line 1360), which monkeypatch.setattr deliberately requires (raising=True): a renamed constant would otherwise let the test run with a 600 s lookahead. It is not a typo, a bad path or a failed control. No C2 assertion is reached against today's code because the three-argument AudioPipe and LOOKAHEAD_SECONDS do not exist yet. The probe in answer 7 shows that against the planned shape the test reaches and passes every judging assertion, and fails each wrong variant at its judging line.\n\n10. Observed expected output: the C1 rows quote today's refusal texts from this run and the cues from the earlier rig probe. Ready for the uncapped inputs is stated as unobserved until the phase is built. Every C2 expected value (48000, (48000, False), 24000\u219232000, 128000, the body bytes, error None) and every wrong-implementation reading (65536, 256000, (24000, 24000), 127999) comes from the probe run, not from reasoning. Where the run differed from my earlier draft (the double-lookahead coincidence), I changed the constants and re-ran.\n</answers>\n\n<exemptions>\nnone\n</exemptions>",
    "step_7_implement:1": "<changes>\n### engine/server/db/jobs/translate-worker.py\n- The `server_config` import no longer takes `SUBTITLE_MAX_BYTES` or `SUBTITLE_MAX_DURATION`.\n- New constant `LOOKAHEAD_SECONDS = 600`: how much decoded audio the reader holds past the translation position.\n- `resolve_video(whitelist_path, video_id, host)` no longer takes `max_duration` and no longer checks the stored duration. It still maps `missing host` to `not in whitelist`. `command_enqueue` and `generate` call it with three arguments.\n- `video_duration` is deleted. In `generate`, the `video duration unknown` failure and the JSON duration check are gone, so a video with any duration, or none, goes on to `pick_media_url`. `generate` builds `AudioPipe(url, media_host(url), max_chunk)` and passes the same `max_chunk` to `translate_audio`.\n- `AudioPipe(url, host, max_chunk)`:\n  - `max_bytes` and `max_samples` are gone. Two new fields, `limit = LOOKAHEAD_SECONDS * SAMPLE_RATE + max_chunk` and `base` (the absolute sample index of `pcm[0]`), are set before the threads start. The old \"all PCM in RAM\" rat-tail comment is replaced.\n  - `_read` waits on `cond` until there is room, `stop` is set or an error is recorded. Each read is `read1(min(READ_CHUNK_BYTES, room))`, so the buffer never goes past `limit` samples. On stop or an error it breaks out and still reaps ffmpeg and sets `done`. The `audio longer than Ns` abort is gone.\n  - `wait_samples` waits for and returns absolute sample counts (`base + len(pcm)//2`).\n  - `slice` takes absolute indices and asserts `start >= base`.\n  - New `release(upto)` drops the samples before `upto`, moves `base` forward and wakes the reader.\n  - `close` wakes a parked reader under `cond` before killing ffmpeg.\n  - `_feed` calls `stream_media(url, host, consume, stop)`.\n- `translate_audio` calls `pipe.release(pos)` right after `pos += cut`.\n- `parse_args` no longer has `enqueue --max-duration`, `run --max-duration` or `run --max-bytes`.\n\n### engine/server/data/source_fetch.py\n- `stream_media(url, host, consume, stop)` no longer takes `max_bytes`. The Content-Length check, the streamed-size check and the `media over N bytes` text are gone, and its docstring says the download is uncapped.\n- The module docstring now says the byte cap applies to `fetch_bounded` only. `fetch_bounded` and `FETCH_MAX_BYTES` are untouched.\n\n### engine/server/api/server_config.py\n- `SUBTITLE_MAX_DURATION` and `SUBTITLE_MAX_BYTES` are removed, with their comments.\n\n### tests/active/test_translate_worker.py\nThree kinds of change: tests that conflict with AC1/AC2 are retired, call sites follow the new signatures, and the docstring is brought in line.\n\n**Retired:**\n- From `BOUNDS`: `JSON duration unknown`, `JSON duration over the cap`, `media Content-Length over max_bytes`, `media streamed past max_bytes` and `decoded audio past max_duration`.\n- From `FETCH_REASONS`: `video JSON served, duration over the cap`.\n- From the enqueue `REFUSALS` and `CONTROL_KEYS`: `stored duration over --max-duration`, along with the `l-1` and `m-1` rows that only it used.\n\n**Follow-on edits:**\n- The bounds test no longer computes `max_bytes`, overrides `max_duration` or checks `unread`.\n- The unused `\"streamed\"` branch of `Rig.serve_media` is removed.\n- `_recording`'s stand-in takes and forwards three arguments.\n- The `Rig.run`, `_serving` and fetch-reasons `Namespace`s carry only `whitelist_db` and `max_chunk_seconds`.\n- The mov test no longer overrides `max_bytes`.\n- `MAX_DURATION` is renamed `JSON_DURATION` (only `_video` uses it).\n- The `REFUSED_STALL_SECONDS` comment now says the flag it was probed on is removed.\n- The module docstring no longer describes the cap cases.\n- The names the checkpoint imports (`rig`, `clip`, `StubRunner`, `ScriptedHost`, `_dispatching_opener`, `_worker`, `MEDIA_URL`, `MEDIA_HOST`, `VIDEO_URL`) are unchanged.\n\n### tests/active/test_source_fetch.py\n- Every `stream_media` call drops the positional `MEDIA_SIZE`. `MEDIA_SIZE` stays as the body size.\n- The three cap tests are retired: `..._refuses_a_declared_length_over_max_bytes_without_reading`, `..._refuses_a_body_streamed_past_max_bytes_consuming_nothing_past_it` and `..._names_its_own_max_bytes`.\n- The docstring and the `MEDIA_SIZE` comment no longer mention `max_bytes` or `media over`.\n\n### tests/tmp/probe_56_phase1_audiopipe.py (throwaway probe, still on disk)\n- This probe imports the edited worker and runs `AudioPipe` with a no-op download, a fake ffmpeg writing 100000 zero bytes, `LOOKAHEAD_SECONDS` 1 and a 1000-sample window.\n- Observed: the reader parked at exactly 34000 bytes (limit 17000 samples) with `done` False. Releasing to the end gave 50000 samples, `done` True, no error, and `close` returned.\n- I have no delete tool, so it needs removing by hand.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\ntests/tmp/probe_56_phase1_audiopipe.py - a throwaway observation probe I wrote and could not delete (I have no delete tool); please remove it.\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",
    "author:tests/tmp/test_56_translate_viewer_lease_uncapped_phase2.py": "<items>\n<item id=\"C1b\">\n<disposition>fixed</disposition>\n<what>Added a second expired queued row, (\"v-expired-late\", 2500, EXPIRED), to QUEUED (:28). This turns red for a claim that drops the head row only when it has expired and then claims the next row, because that claim leaves v-expired-late queued. The :75 control pins it as (\"queued\", EXPIRED) before the claim. WHERE state IN ('queued','running') AND wanted_at <= ?`, which deletes the row (KeyError at :88, wrong set at :89). It also turns red for any rewrite of the running row's columns. The setup claim runs at 600, so a default cutoff derived from that clock cannot reach 820_000 and drop the row during setup. The docstring sentence now says the job \"has fetched the video JSON and opened the media (so the abandon came in the chunk loop, not before it)\".</what>\n</item>\n</items>\n\n<findings_addressed>\nClaim CRITICAL 1 (C1, :75, the only expired row is the head): added v-expired-late, queued behind v-unleased with the cutoff lease, and :83 asserts it is deleted. :89's survivor set excludes it.\nClaim CRITICAL 2 (C1, :79, only a `ready` member of \"non-queued\" is checked): added v-running, claimed before the rest are queued and carrying the cutoff lease. :88 asserts it is byte-identical after the claim, and :89 asserts it survives, so a `state IN ('queued','running')` sweep turns red.\nClaim RECOMMENDATION 1 (D2b, :105): taken. :114 asserts the instance and media URLs were opened (values observed by a probe), so an abandon before the chunk loop turns red. Docstring updated to match.\nClaim RECOMMENDATION 2 (lease-length bounds on the running side): not taken. The test states no lease length (C2 names none), and the claim side's exact boundary at :24-26 already covers the comparison.\n</findings_addressed>\n\n<rows>\n<row clause=\"C1\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_56_translate_viewer_lease_uncapped_phase2.py:82, :83, :84, :85, :86, :87, :88, :89 \u2014 after `claim_translate_job(conn, \"en\", 1_000_000, expired_at=820_000)`, these lines check the following. :82, :83: both queued rows leased exactly on the cutoff are gone (v-expired, at the head, and v-expired-late, behind v-unleased). :84: the claimed job is v-unleased. :85: the unleased row is running with started_at 1_000_000 and attempts 1, every other column (its NULL lease included) unchanged. :86, :87, :88: the fresh, ready and running rows are byte-identical. :89: exactly {v-running, v-unleased, v-fresh, v-ready} remain.</assertion>\n<expected>v-expired and v-expired-late are absent. The job is (\"v-unleased\", peer.example, 1_000_000, 1). The v-fresh, v-ready and v-running rows equal their pre-claim snapshots, rowid included.</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>A claim that deletes the head row only if it has expired, then claims the next one, leaves v-expired-late queued, so :83 is red. A `<` comparison keeps v-expired, so :82 is red. A claim with no drop takes v-expired, so :82 and :84 are red. `COALESCE(wanted_at,0) <= ?` deletes v-unleased, so :84 and :85 are red. A cutoff check that is missing or off by one deletes v-fresh, so :86 is red. A delete with no state filter deletes v-ready, so :87 is red. A `state IN ('queued','running')` sweep deletes v-running, so :88 and :89 are red.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C2\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_56_translate_viewer_lease_uncapped_phase2.py:112, :113, :114, :115, :116, :128, :129, :131 \u2014 lease 1000 with now_ms = 10**13: :112 the row is gone, :113 exactly one `abandoned, no viewer` line is logged, :114 the instance and media URLs were opened, :115 there were zero transcribes, :116 run_job returned False. Whole claim: yes, but every clause is carried. C1 has the expired drop at line 75, the oldest survivor at 76, unleased kept at 77, fresh kept at 78, non-queued kept at 79 and nothing else touched at 80. C2's lapsed half (row deleted, one abandoned line, first wake, False) is at lines 103-106. Its unleased half is at 118, 119 and 121, with a current-lease twin. The defect was in the docstring: it claimed the Abandon tests go through `Rig.claim(wanted_at=...)`, a signature the harness does not have. Rewritten: the docstring now says v-1 is enqueued and claimed with the store's own functions on rig.conn.\n2. Absence only: there was one. Line 121's empty abandoned-line list had no proof that caplog sees the worker's info lines. Added line 120, which asserts the observed \"[translate-worker] job ready video_id=v-1 host=peer.example\" is in caplog. The other absence assertions are armed. \"v-expired not in after\" (75) is armed by the control at 68, which sees it stored queued with wanted_at 820000. rig.row() == {} (103) is armed by _claim's control at 88 (running, lease 1000). transcribes == 0 (105) is armed by the probe's 2 transcribes on the same clip.\n3. Echoed literal: no. The before/after comparisons at 77-79 compare the store's own rows across the claim, and the test performs no SQL of its own. The production lines whose deletion turns them red are the planned claim DELETE in claim_translate_job (75, 76, 80), its `wanted_at IS NOT NULL` (77), its `<= ?` cutoff (78) and its `state='queued'` gate (79). For C2 it is translate_audio's lease check plus run_job's JobAbandoned branch (103-106), and abandon's NOT NULL / lease-length predicate (118). CLIP_CUES was observed, not computed.\n4. One value: no. The cutoff is read on both sides of the boundary: 820000 is expired and 820001 is fresh. NULL and a non-queued state are separate inputs. The worker is run at three leases (lapsed 1000, NULL, and current at 10**13), all against one far clock, so the lease length is never pinned.\n5. The double: no. StubRunner stands in for WhisperRunner (the GPU/model layer), ScriptedHost stands in for the network, and worker.now_ms is the clock. Store, worker, ffmpeg and sqlite are all real.\n6. It collects: the first version did not. It collected 4 items, but `Rig.claim()` has no `wanted_at` parameter (test_translate_worker.py:530 is `claim(self, video_id=\"v-1\", host=HOST)`), so three tests died on the harness's TypeError. Rewritten with a local `_claim(rig, lease)` that mirrors Rig.claim through enqueue_translate_job and claim_translate_job on rig.conn. QUEUED_AT, STARTED_AT and Rig are imported from test_translate_worker, and each exists there (lines 164, 165, 493). The run collected 4 items: 1 claim test, 1 lapsed test, and 2 parametrized cases, which matches what I wrote.\n7. Observed, not predicted: probe tests/tmp/probe_56_phase2_observe.py was run with -s. Seen: today's claim on the four rows claims v-expired and changes only state, started_at and attempts. store_ready_subtitles over a queued row keeps queued_at and attempts. The unleased run at now_ms 10**13 ends ready/whisper with exactly CLIP_CUES, 2 transcribes, returns False, and logs \"[translate-worker] job ready video_id=v-1 host=peer.example\". Not observable before the phase: the `wanted_at` column, the abandon log text and the abandon path. The substring \"abandoned, no viewer\" is the plan's specified log text, so I only count it rather than pinning the full line. The build's post-implementation run of this file is what confirms it. I could not delete the probe because I have no delete tool. tests/tmp/probe_56_phase2_observe.py is outside this step's files and needs removing by hand.\n8. Red, not green: yes. ValidateTests exited 1: \"4 failed\", with \"collected 4 items\" and FFFF.\n9. Red for the right reason: before the rewrite, no. Three of four failed on \"TypeError: Rig.claim() got an unexpected keyword argument 'wanted_at'\", which is the harness, not the code. After the rewrite, every red lands on the first use of this phase's own lease, which the plan adds to engine/server/data/subtitles.py:\n- Line 64 (via _enqueue at line 56) fails on \"E   TypeError: enqueue_translate_job() got an unexpected keyword argument 'wanted_at'\" for the claim test, and the same error comes through _claim (line 85) for [lapsed] and [lease stamped now].\n- Line 88, the _claim control, fails on \"E   KeyError: 'wanted_at'\" for [unleased], because the column is not yet in JOB_COLUMNS.\n\n  None of these is a typo, a missing import, a missing path or a harness gap. But to be plain, none reaches a judging assertion either, and no seam can: the lease column and keyword are the thing being built, and every C1/C2 setup has to store a lease or read the column. I chose a strict `row[\"wanted_at\"]` control over a `.get` that would pass vacuously on a missing column. That keeps the control real after implementation, at the cost of the unleased case failing on that control today.\n10. Observed expected output: each row's expected value is either seen in the probe run or follows from it. That covers v-expired being claimed by today's claim, the claim touching only state, started_at and attempts, the ready row keeping its job columns, CLIP_CUES, transcribes 2, False, and the job ready line. The checkpoint run itself showed only the setup TypeError and KeyError quoted in 9, so it neither confirmed nor contradicted any row. The two values that rest on the plan rather than on a run are noted in 7: the \"abandoned, no viewer\" substring and the 0 transcribes at the first wake.\n</answers>\n\n<exemptions>\nnone\n</exemptions>",
    "step_7_implement:2": "<changes>\n### engine/server/data/subtitles.py\n- `JOB_COLUMNS` gains `(\"wanted_at\", \"INTEGER\")`. The existing in-place `ALTER` loop in `ensure_subtitles_schema` adds it, and rows from before the migration read NULL, which means unleased.\n- `enqueue_translate_job(..., queued_at, *, wanted_at: int | None = None)` writes `wanted_at` on insert. Every positional caller, including the CLI, still inserts NULL.\n- `claim_translate_job(conn, target_language, started_at, *, expired_at: int | None = None)`: when `expired_at` is given, the existing `_immediate` block first runs `DELETE ... WHERE state = 'queued' AND target_language = ? AND wanted_at IS NOT NULL AND wanted_at <= ?`, then claims the oldest remaining row as before. Running, ready, unleased and fresh rows are never touched. With no cutoff, behaviour is unchanged.\n- Two new `TranslateJob` methods:\n  - `read_lease()` reads `wanted_at` only while the row is still `running` with this claim's `started_at`. It returns None for a CLI job or once the claim is lost, so a row the instance track took over never shows its stale lease.\n  - `abandon(expired_at)` is one conditional DELETE on the key, `state = 'running'`, the claim's `started_at`, `wanted_at IS NOT NULL` and `wanted_at <= expired_at`, under `with self.conn:`. It returns `rowcount == 1`. It is a sibling of `_update_claim` and does not go through it, because it deletes rather than updates.\n- The module docstring, the `JOB_COLUMNS` comment and the `TranslateJob` docstring now mention the lease column, the claim's drop and the two new methods.\n\n### engine/server/db/jobs/translate-worker.py\n- The `server_config` import gains `TRANSLATE_LEASE_MS`. The api/ path comment and the module docstring mention the lease.\n- New `JobAbandoned` exception.\n- New `lease_lapsed(job)`: it takes `expired_at = now_ms() - TRANSLATE_LEASE_MS`, and returns True only when `read_lease()` gives a non-NULL lease at or before that cutoff and `abandon(expired_at)` deleted the row.\n  - A `sqlite3.Error` is logged as a warning and counts as not lapsed, so a locked store never fails a viewer's job.\n  - A renewal that wins the race against the delete also counts as not lapsed, and the job carries on with its cues. This is the operator's \"continue\" decision.\n- `translate_audio` checks `lease_lapsed(job)` at every wake, right after the `stop` check, and raises `JobAbandoned`. That puts the check after the whitelist, instance-track and video-JSON fetches and the media open, and before any chunk is transcribed.\n- `run_job` gets a new `except JobAbandoned` branch that logs `[translate-worker] abandoned, no viewer video_id=%s host=%s` once and returns False. Its docstring names the abandon path.\n- `serve` claims with `expired_at=now - TRANSLATE_LEASE_MS`, using one `now_ms()` for both the claim time and the cutoff.\n\n### engine/server/api/server_config.py\n- Adds `TRANSLATE_LEASE_MS = 180_000` beside the other translate constants, with a one-line comment. The approved plan has this constant, but Phase 1 did not land it, and the worker needs it here.\n\n### tests/active/test_subtitles.py\n- These edits follow from the new column, which is a confirmed requirement (the plan's \"JOB_COLUMN_NAMES gains wanted_at\"):\n  - `JOB_COLUMN_NAMES` gains `wanted_at`, so `ALL_COLUMNS` has fifteen columns.\n  - The upgrade test's NULL check on the old rows also covers `wanted_at`.\n  - The `end_ready_from_instance` full-row dict gains `\"wanted_at\": None`.\n  - The docstring counts are updated (\"six nullable job columns\", \"fifteen columns\") and the column list names `wanted_at`.\n- No assertion was loosened. Each one still checks the exact schema and row, now with the extra column.\n\n### tests/active/test_translate_worker.py\n- Not changed. The checkpoint claims through the store's own `claim_translate_job`, so `Rig.claim` needed no `wanted_at`. Existing Rig and serve tests queue unleased rows, which are never dropped or abandoned.\n\n### tests/active/test_internal_translate.py\n- `QUEUED_ROW`, compared against `SELECT *`, gains a trailing `None` for the new `wanted_at` column. In this phase the Engine's enqueue route does not stamp a lease yet; Phase 3 makes that element `NOW`.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\nengine/server/api/server_config.py: added `TRANSLATE_LEASE_MS = 180_000`. The worker's lease cutoff needs it, the approved design puts it in server_config, and no phase lists server_config except Phase 1, which did not add it.\ntests/active/test_internal_translate.py: `QUEUED_ROW` is a 14-tuple compared against `SELECT *`. Adding the `wanted_at` column in this phase makes it 15 columns, so I appended `None` (the route does not stamp a lease until Phase 3). Without this, five enqueue-route tests (lines 1095, 1110, 1123, 1159, 1174) go red on the schema change alone.\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",

    "step_7_implement:3": "<changes>\nPaths below are the real ones. The phase list's `client/engine_api_client.py`, `client/server.py` and `tests/fixtures/translate_contract.json` are `client/backend/lib/engine_api_client.py`, `client/backend/server.py` and `tests/active/fixtures/translate_contract.json`.\n\n### engine/server/api/handlers/internal_translate.py\n- **Renewal on read:** `_read_key` now renews the lease when the row it read is `queued` or `running`. It calls `renew_translate_lease(conn, key\u2026, now_ms())` inside the same `subtitles_db_lock` hold as the read. The renewal has its own `try/except sqlite3.Error`, which logs `[translate] lease renewal failed video_id=\u2026 host=\u2026` and returns the answer unchanged. A renewal error therefore never reads as \"no row\" and never ends the page's poll. Ready, failed, already_english and missing rows cost no write.\n- **Enqueue stamps the lease:** `handle_internal_translate_enqueue` passes `wanted_at=now` with the same `now_ms()` used for `queued_at`. Phase 2 left this to Phase 3. Without it, no page job would carry a lease, and renewal and cancel would never match a row.\n- **New `handle_internal_translate_cancel`:**\n  - It calls `_resolve_translate_key`, so a bad body answers 400 and an unknown or denied video answers 404, exactly as the other two routes do.\n  - In one `_subtitles_store` hold it calls `cancel_translate_lease(..., now_ms() - TRANSLATE_LEASE_MS + TRANSLATE_CANCEL_GRACE_MS)`, then `fetch_subtitle_state` and `_generation_available`.\n  - It answers `{state, available}` with no cues, using `none` for no row.\n  - A closed store answers `{none, false}`. A `sqlite3.Error` is logged and answers 503 `Translate store unavailable`.\n- **Imports:** `cancel_translate_lease`, `renew_translate_lease`, `TRANSLATE_CANCEL_GRACE_MS` and `TRANSLATE_LEASE_MS`.\n- **Docstrings:**\n  - The module docstring describes renewal, the lease taken at enqueue, and a new cancel-route paragraph. \"Stores only ready\" now reads \"stores only ready and renews leases\".\n  - `resolve_translatable_video` and `_resolve_translate_key` now say all three routes.\n  - The enqueue docstring names the lease.\n\n### engine/server/api/router.py\n- Imports `handle_internal_translate_cancel`.\n- Adds `POST_ROUTES[\"/internal/translate/cancel\"]`. The existing `/internal/` gate covers it.\n- Adds a `[bridge gate]` line for the route to the module docstring.\n\n### engine/server/api/handlers/__init__.py\n- The `internal_translate` line now names the cancel bridge request.\n\n### engine/server/api/server_config.py (not in this phase's list)\n- Adds `TRANSLATE_CANCEL_GRACE_MS = 20_000` with a one-line comment: it must stay above the page's 16 s `STATE_POLL_MAX_MS`.\n\n### engine/server/data/subtitles.py (not in this phase's list)\n- New `_LEASED` predicate: `state IN ('queued','running') AND wanted_at IS NOT NULL`.\n- New `renew_translate_lease(conn, key\u2026, now)`: one conditional UPDATE under `with conn:` that sets `wanted_at = now`.\n- New `cancel_translate_lease(conn, key\u2026, capped_at)`: the same predicate, with `wanted_at = MIN(wanted_at, ?)`, so it never lengthens a lease.\n- The module docstring names both functions and says CLI rows are never renewed or shortened.\n\n### client/backend/lib/engine_api_client.py\n- New `cancel_translate(engine_base_url, video_id, host)`, a mirror of `request_translate`:\n  - one POST of `{id, host}` to `/internal/translate/cancel`, with the default 6 s timeout and the bridge headers;\n  - a 404 `Video not found` maps to `{none, false}`;\n  - any other non-200 raises `Engine translate cancel failed (HTTP N): \u2026`;\n  - the state must be in `TRANSLATE_STATES`, so `busy` raises `Engine translate cancel returned invalid payload`;\n  - `available` goes through `_translate_available`.\n- The `TRANSLATE_REQUEST_STATES` comment notes that the cancel route answers `TRANSLATE_STATES`.\n\n### client/backend/server.py\n- `_handle_translate_post` now takes the Engine call as a parameter, `engine_call: Callable[[str, str, str], dict[str, Any]]`. The profile check, the body read after it, the validation and `_respond_engine_failure(\"translate\", \u2026)` are shared as they were.\n- `/api/translate` passes `request_translate`.\n- A new `/api/translate/cancel` branch in `_serve_post`, placed before the 404, runs `_rate_limit_check(url.path)` (its own bucket, 429), then `_handle_translate_post(cancel_translate)`.\n- The import adds `cancel_translate`.\n\n### client/frontend/src/data/translate.ts\n- New exported `cancelTranslate(apiBase, id, host)`, which POSTs `{id, host}` to `/api/translate/cancel`.\n- `requestTranslate` and `cancelTranslate` now share a private `postTranslate(apiBase, path, id, host, states)`. It holds the old `requestTranslate` body with the path and the accepted state list as parameters.\n- New `CANCEL_STATES` (the six stored states). `REQUEST_STATES` is now `[...CANCEL_STATES, \"busy\"]`, so `busy` on cancel throws `Translate response was malformed`.\n- New type `TranslateCancelState`, and the module comment names the cancel.\n\n### tests/active/fixtures/translate_contract.json\n- Adds 17 `cancel` cases:\n  - the six stored states, each with and without `available`;\n  - one `cancel video not found` 404 \u2192 `{none, false}`;\n  - rejected: `cancel route missing 404`, `cancel busy`, `cancel unknown state`, `cancel available a string`.\n- No cancel case carries cues.\n- The description names the third route and the three gateway functions.\n\n### tests/active/test_engine_api_client.py\n- `ROUTES` gains `cancel`, and the import gains `cancel_translate`.\n- The replay dispatches through a small `_gateway_call(case, engine_base)`.\n- The coverage loop adds `(\"cancel\", TRANSLATE_STATES)`.\n- The module and test docstrings now cover three routes.\n\n### tests/active/test_internal_translate.py\n- `QUEUED_ROW`'s last element (`wanted_at`) is now `NOW`, the lease the enqueue route takes.\n- New `_cancel_driver(row)` with six `(\"cancel\", state)` entries in `ENGINE_DRIVERS`.\n- `ROUTE_STATES` adds the six cancel pairs, making 19.\n- `HANDLERS[\"cancel\"] = \"handle_internal_translate_cancel\"`.\n- The startup test also POSTs `/internal/translate/cancel` with the token (expects 404 `Video not found`) and without it (expects 401).\n- The docstrings are updated, including the pair count, the enqueue row's lease, the cancel drivers and `_record_handlers`.\n\n### tests/active/test_frontend_translate.py (not in this phase's list)\n- `CONTRACT_RUNNER` imports `cancelTranslate` and sends cancel cases through it.\n- `_result`'s request control expects path `/api/translate/cancel` for a cancel case.\n- The docstrings are updated to match.\n\n### tests/config.json\n- `test_internal_translate.py` now also maps to `engine/server/api/router.py`.\n\n### tests/active/test_server.py\n- Not changed. The checkpoint covers the gateway cancel route (one bridge call, the answer mapping, 401 with no call) through the helpers already in this file.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\nengine/server/api/server_config.py - added `TRANSLATE_CANCEL_GRACE_MS = 20_000`. The cancel cap needs it, the approved design puts it in server_config, and no phase lists server_config for it.\nengine/server/data/subtitles.py - added `renew_translate_lease` and `cancel_translate_lease` (and the `_LEASED` predicate) as the design names them. Phase 2 did not add them, and every store write lives in this module.\ntests/active/test_frontend_translate.py - the new `cancel` fixture cases would otherwise replay through `requestTranslate`, and `cancel busy` would come back as a value instead of a throw. That is the fixture-and-three-replayers-land-together risk the impact list names. I changed only `CONTRACT_RUNNER`'s dispatch and import, `_result`'s expected path, and their docstrings. Phase 4's scenarios are untouched.\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",

    "step_7_implement:4": "<changes>\n### `client/frontend/src/pages/video-page/translate.ts`\n- **C1: cancel on turnOff.** Each translate request the page sends is now wrapped in a new `tracked()` helper. That covers turnOn's state read, every state poll and every generation request. `tracked()` extends a module-level `requestsSettled` promise, built with `Promise.allSettled(...).then(() => undefined)` so earlier answers don't pile up inside it. `turnOff` now takes `(apiBase, video)` and sends `cancelTranslate` (which already existed in `data/translate.ts`) once `requestsSettled` resolves. So with nothing in flight the cancel goes out on the next microtask, and with a poll in flight it waits for that poll's answer. A failed cancel is caught. The comment explains why there is nothing to show: the lease runs out on its own and the page is already off. The click handler passes `apiBase` and `video` through.\n- **C2: re-request from the poll.** turnOn's existing \"none + available \u2192 `requestTranslate` \u2192 `applyRequest`\" branch moved into a new `applyFetched()`, which turnOn and the state poll now share. The poll changed from `.then(ok, err)` to `.then(applyFetched).catch(err)`, so a failed re-request takes the same path as a failed poll: a 401 shows its message, and anything else retries with backoff. `applyFetched` sets `lastState = \"none\"` before the request, so the `queued` answer for the new job counts as a change and the poll restarts at 2 s instead of carrying on the old job's doubled delay.\n- Updated the module doc comment to cover both behaviours.\n\n### `tests/active/test_frontend_translate.py`\n- Retired the `stop-none` case. Its `none` answer used the default `available: true`, and it asserted that this answer ends the poll, which C2 now contradicts. With C2 that `none` sends a generation request (answered 500 in that runner) and the poll retries. I removed the `stop-none` scenario, dropped `\"none\"` from the parametrization, renamed the test to `test_a_401_or_turning_translate_off_ends_the_poll`, and updated the docstring line. A `none` *without* `available` still ends the poll; the existing `unavailable` scenario and the checkpoint's `re-request-unavailable` twin both cover it.\n- Nothing else in the file conflicts. Both runners answer `/api/translate/cancel` with a fallback 200 `{}`, which `cancelTranslate` rejects as malformed and the page catches. The assertions there filter on the exact `/api/translate` path.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\nnone\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",
    "step_8_i1_refactor": "<refactors>\nclient/backend/lib/engine_api_client.py: request_translate and cancel_translate were near-copies of each other. Both now call one private _post_translate(engine_base_url, route, operation, video_id, host, states), the backend twin of the frontend's postTranslate. Each error text stays as it was: \"Engine translate request|cancel failed (HTTP N): \u2026\" and \"\u2026 returned invalid payload\".\nengine/server/data/subtitles.py: new _CLAIMED predicate (key, state 'running', claim's started_at) beside _KEY and _LEASED. _update_claim, TranslateJob.read_lease and TranslateJob.abandon now all use it instead of three copies of the same WHERE clause.\n</refactors>\n\n<left_out>\nI didn't run either refactor; you asked me not to run suites. Both are behaviour-preserving by construction: same SQL text after f-string expansion, same error strings and same states sets. The gates that cover them are test_engine_api_client.py, test_server.py, test_subtitles.py and test_translate_worker.py.\nclient/backend/server.py: the /api/analytics/event, /api/translate and /api/translate/cancel branches repeat the same rate-limit-then-429 block. That pattern is the file's existing style for every POST branch, so folding three of them would be a cross-cutting change to unrelated routes.\ntranslate-worker.py, source_fetch.py, server_config.py, internal_translate.py, router.py and both translate.ts files: I found nothing to simplify that wasn't just a cosmetic rewrite.\nDocs still describe the removed caps: DEPLOYMENT.md lines 236, 279-280 and 290 (--max-duration, --max-bytes, SUBTITLE_MAX_DURATION/BYTES), and per the plan's docs checklist TRANSLATE_WORKER.md and engine/server/README.md too. These are documentation, not production code, so they belong to the docs step and not this pass.\nThrowaway probes from phases 1-4 are still on disk in tests/tmp/: probe_56_*.py and the test_56_translate_viewer_lease_uncapped_phase*.py files. I have no delete tool, so they need removing by hand.\n</left_out>\n\n<needs_fresh_red>\nnone\n</needs_fresh_red>\n\n<observation>\nThe four phases came together cleanly; this pass only removed duplication: one shared translate-POST helper in the Client's Engine client, and one claim predicate in the store. Neither changes behaviour; they are unverified by a run, as no suite was run.\n</observation>",
    "step_8_triage:0": "<failures>\n### tests.active.test_frontend_dist::test_the_committed_dist_holds_exactly_the_assets_a_fresh_build_emits_and_no_about_override\n**Cause.** The committed `client/frontend/dist/` was stale. Phase 3 changed `src/data/translate.ts` and Phase 4 changed `src/pages/video-page/translate.ts`, and neither rebuilt `dist/`. A fresh build emits `video-TGMMB96m.js` while the committed dist still had `video-Cbu0t9sB.js`. The plan's impact list had flagged this file (\"an unbuilt dist/ serves the old page: no cancel, no AC6\").\n\n**Test or implementation?** The implementation, as a missing build step. The test is sound and its docstring requires a rebuild after any source change.\n\n**What I changed.** I rebuilt `dist/` using the frontend's own `vite build` from a throwaway probe. I saw it exit 0 with an empty stderr and no `could not be resolved` warning. It emitted `video-TGMMB96m.js`, the name the failing run's fresh build produced. No other asset name changed.\n\n### tests.active.test_frontend_translate::test_a_none_state_without_a_serving_worker_sends_no_request_polls_nothing_and_reads_the_plan_48_message\n**Cause.** The test fails on its control: `assert len(_translate_by_method(twin, \"POST\")) == 1` got 4. The `\"available\"` twin scenario serves `none` with `available: true` to every GET, because the stub repeats its last answer. Before this build, a `none` on the poll ended the poll after the single turn-on POST. Under AC6, which is Phase 4's C2 and a confirmed requirement, every poll-path `none` with `available` sends another generation request. So the twin re-POSTs about every 2 s across its 6.5 s wait, and 4 POSTs is the correct behaviour. Its unavailable-page assertions are never reached.\n\n**Test or implementation?** Neither one is wrong in the usual sense. The test was right before the build and now conflicts with a confirmed requirement. The page does what AC6 says, so the implementation needs no change.\n\n**What I changed.** I retired the test whole, together with the two `GENERATION_SCENARIOS` entries only it read (`\"unavailable\"` and `\"available\"`) and its line in the module docstring. They went to `tests/archive/57_translate_viewer_lease_uncapped/test_frontend_translate.py`, verbatim, under a header that says why. I did not repoint it: the plan's impact list proposed changing the twin's GETs to `[none, queued]`, but that would edit an already-gated control to fit the new behaviour.\n\nWhat still covers this ground:\n- `test_a_none_state_reads_no_english_translation_and_a_reported_position_shows_nothing`: a turn-on `none` without `available` makes one request and shows the message.\n- `test_a_none_state_from_a_serving_worker_sends_one_generation_request_...`: a turn-on `none` with `available` sends exactly one POST.\n- Phase 4's `re-request-unavailable` twin: a poll-path `none` without `available` sends no further POST.\n\nWhat is lost is the flag-only twin comparison at turn-on.\n\n### tests.active.test_random_cache::test_positive_interval_swaps_a_new_file_in_each_tick_while_the_random_feed_serves_the_current_one\n**Cause.** One random-feed request was answered 500 with no rows (`(500, 0)`) while cache files were being swapped. Nothing in this build is on that path. The build changed translate handlers, one added `POST_ROUTES` entry in `router.py`, the subtitles store, the translate worker and the frontend translate modules; it did not touch random-cache build, swap or read code. The same `(500, 0)` from this same test was triaged in build 51-48 as load from the parallel run, where every lane starts its own Engine on one `whitelist.db` and the 5 s statement deadline answers 500.\n\n**Not observed this time:** that run's `engine.log` sits under a pytest tmp dir I cannot read. A statement-deadline traceback in it, or the test going green in a less loaded re-run, would confirm the cause.\n\n**Test or implementation?** Neither in this build. The test does not conflict with any requirement here. I did not edit or retire it.\n</failures>\n\n<checkpoint_gaps>\n**Phase 4 (Page cancel and re-request), the stale dist.** Phase 4 is the last phase to change frontend sources (Phase 3 also changed `data/translate.ts`). Its checkpoint bundles the TypeScript sources with esbuild in a tmp runner, so it never looks at the committed `dist/`, and the phase closed without the rebuild the plan's impact list called for. Nothing in any phase gate runs `test_frontend_dist.py`.\n\n**Phase 4, the missed conflict.** Phase 4's outcome says \"Nothing else in the file conflicts\" after it retired `stop-none`. The plan's impact list had already named the `\"available\"` scenario as broken by AC6 (\"now re-POSTs repeatedly \u2026 breaks `len(POST) == 1`\"). Phase 4's checkpoint ran only `tests/tmp/test_56_translate_viewer_lease_uncapped_phase4.py`. It never ran the durable `generation_pages` tests in `tests/active/test_frontend_translate.py` that sit on the same seam and that Phase 4 had itself edited. One run of that file would have caught this test.\n\n**A plan decision missing from every phase, found in reading and not red in this run.** These are predictions from reading `client/frontend/src/pages/video-page/translate.ts`; I did not observe them:\n- **Possible request spin.** The plan (AC6 design, and the item \"A poll-path re-request follows up with the backoff delay, not 0\") requires a poll-path re-request to follow up with the doubling `stateDelay`. The code instead sends it through `applyRequest`, which calls `scheduleStatePoll(..., 0)` for an enqueue answer of `ready` or `running`. Take a ready row whose cues fail to load: it reads `none` on the state route and `ready` on enqueue. That row would make GET+POST pairs with no delay between them, which is the spin the plan's backoff rule exists to prevent. A scenario with GETs `[none]` and POSTs `[ready]` would show it.\n- **Recommendation 1 not implemented.** The plan's operator-taken Recommendation 1 is: keep polling queued/running at `STATE_POLL_MAX_MS` while `available` is false. It is not implemented; `if (!state.available) return;` still ends the poll.\n\nNo phase's clauses cover either item, so no checkpoint could have caught them. I did not fix them, because a fix would land ungated. They need a phase and a test of their own.\n\n**Phases 1 and 4, tests deleted without archiving.** The tests Phases 1 and 4 retired (the `gone` entries in `test_translate_worker`, `test_source_fetch` and `stop-none`) were deleted rather than copied to `tests/archive/` as earlier builds did. That is not a red, but those tests now have no archive record.\n\n**`test_random_cache`:** no gap. No phase of this build touches that path.\n</checkpoint_gaps>\n\n<correction>\nThe suite should now be down to the `test_random_cache` failure, which I left alone as unrelated to this build. Nothing has been re-run yet.\n\n1. I read `tests/last_test_output.txt` and `tests/last_test_validation.json`. There were three failures. The `gone` and `appeared` entries are the retirements from Phases 1 and 4 and the new Phase 3 cancel cases; they are expected.\n2. **Rebuilt `client/frontend/dist/`.** This file is not named in my step. The dist test requires the rebuild, and build 59's step 8 did the same. I ran `vite build` in `client/frontend` from the probe `tests/tmp/probe_57_rebuild_dist.py`. It exited 0, wrote nothing to stderr, and printed no unresolved-import warning. The only changed asset name is `video-Cbu0t9sB.js`, now `video-TGMMB96m.js`, which matches the fresh build in the failing run. No source was changed after the rebuild.\n3. **Retired the frontend test.** I removed `test_a_none_state_without_a_serving_worker_sends_no_request_polls_nothing_and_reads_the_plan_48_message` from `tests/active/test_frontend_translate.py`, along with its `\"unavailable\"` and `\"available\"` `GENERATION_SCENARIOS` entries and its module-docstring line. The verbatim excerpts, with the reason, are in `tests/archive/57_translate_viewer_lease_uncapped/test_frontend_translate.py`. Nothing else in the file changed, and no remaining test reads the removed scenarios.\n4. **`test_random_cache`:** not edited, not retired, no production change. This build does not touch the path, and the same failure was attributed to load in build 51-48.\n5. I touched no checkpoint and no gated test other than the one I retired, and I made no production code change.\n\n**Operator actions:**\n- Commit the rebuilt `client/frontend/dist/`.\n- Delete `tests/tmp/probe_57_rebuild_dist.py`. I have no delete tool, so I reduced it to a one-line note.\n- Delete the earlier throwaway files still on disk: `tests/tmp/probe_56_phase1_audiopipe.py`, `tests/tmp/probe_56_phase3_engine.py`, `tests/tmp/probe_56_phase4_checkpoint.py` and `tests/tmp/probe_59_rebuild_dist.py`.\n- Decide whether the two gaps in `checkpoint_gaps` get their own phase: the possible delay-0 spin after a poll-path re-request answered `ready`/`running`, and Recommendation 1, which is not implemented.\n- If `test_random_cache` is red again, check that lane's `engine.log` for a statement-deadline traceback, or re-run with fewer lanes.\n</correction>",

    "step_9_triage": "<docs>\n<doc path=\"engine/server/db/jobs/docs/TRANSLATE_WORKER.md\" update=\"yes\">\nThis document still describes the duration and size caps, which are gone. What has to change:\n- **Job Lifecycle.** The queued row carries `wanted_at` when it was queued from the page. \"Every job ends in exactly one of\u2026\" gains the abandoned path: a leased job whose lease lapsed is deleted at claim while queued, or deleted at a chunk-loop wake while running. It leaves no row, reads `none` and can be queued again. \"A failed key is never queued again\" stays.\n- **Enqueue.** Remove `--max-duration`, \"the worker adds the stored `duration`\" and the `refused: duration Ns over Ms` outcome. Say that the Engine's enqueue route stamps `wanted_at` (the viewer lease) and that CLI jobs carry NULL and run to the end.\n- **Run flags.** Only `--max-chunk-seconds` remains; `--max-duration` and `--max-bytes` are gone.\n- **Serve Loop.** Each pass runs the job until it ends or is abandoned. The claim takes `expired_at = now - TRANSLATE_LEASE_MS` and, in the same IMMEDIATE transaction, first deletes queued leased rows at or before that cutoff. The drop is silent: no log line was added.\n- **Job Pipeline.**\n  - Delete \"Check its duration\". A video with any JSON duration, or none, goes on to `pick_media_url`.\n  - Replace the statement that all PCM stays in memory (about 115 MB at the 60-minute cap) with the bound. `AudioPipe` holds at most `LOOKAHEAD_SECONDS` (600 s) past the translation position plus one window (`--max-chunk-seconds`), about 20 MB. `translate_audio` releases the samples behind `pos` after each window. When the buffer is full, `_read` parks and ffmpeg and the download wait.\n  - While the buffer is parked the socket is not read, so a media host's send timeout can end the job `media download failed`.\n- **Bounds.** Delete the Duration and Media size rows. Add a Lookahead row (`LOOKAHEAD_SECONDS`, a worker constant) and a Viewer lease row (`TRANSLATE_LEASE_MS` 180 s, `TRANSLATE_CANCEL_GRACE_MS` 20 s).\n- **Error Texts.** Remove `duration Ns over Ms`, `video duration unknown`, `media over N bytes` and `audio longer than Ns`.\n- **New section, Viewer Lease and Cancel.**\n  - Every Engine state read of a queued or running leased row renews `wanted_at`.\n  - The claim drops queued rows whose lease has lapsed.\n  - At every wake, `translate_audio` checks `lease_lapsed` right after the stop check, which happens after the media open and before any chunk is transcribed. `read_lease` only reads while the claim holds. On expiry the worker runs `abandon`, one conditional DELETE.\n  - A renewal that wins the race against the delete lets the job continue with its cues.\n  - A `sqlite3.Error` on the read or the delete is logged as a warning and counts as not lapsed.\n  - A cancel caps the lease at the 20 s grace and never lengthens it.\n  - CLI rows (NULL) are never renewed, shortened, dropped or abandoned.\n  - SIGTERM requeues and keeps `wanted_at`. Recovery requeues as before, and a lease that lapsed while the worker was down is dropped at the next claim.\n- **Stop.** `close` wakes a reader parked on a full lookahead. A feeder blocked writing is released when ffmpeg is killed.\n- **Takeover.** The six methods gain `read_lease` and `abandon`. `abandon` is a conditional DELETE on the claim.\n- **Logs.** Add the info line `[translate-worker] abandoned, no viewer video_id=\u2026 host=\u2026`.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"engine/server/README.md\" update=\"yes\">\n- **Line 3:** the subtitles.db writers include `/internal/translate/cancel`.\n- **Cache (line 24):**\n  - The job columns gain `wanted_at`.\n  - \"The route stores only ready\" becomes \"stores only ready and renews a leased queued or running row's `wanted_at` in the same `subtitles_db_lock` hold\". A renewal failure logs `[translate] lease renewal failed` and leaves the answer unchanged.\n- **Line 28:** a new enqueued job carries `wanted_at = now`.\n- **Line 31:** delete the **Duration** bullet. The worker no longer checks duration.\n- **New `POST /internal/translate/cancel {id, host}` bullet:**\n  - bridge-gated, with the same 400 and 404 `Video not found` answers;\n  - one conditional `cancel_translate_lease` that sets `wanted_at = MIN(wanted_at, now - lease + grace)` on leased queued or running rows only;\n  - answers `{state, available}` with no cues, using `none` for no row;\n  - a store error answers 503 `Translate store unavailable`, and a closed store answers `{none, false}`.\n- **Line 35:** the tunables drop `SUBTITLE_MAX_DURATION` and `SUBTITLE_MAX_BYTES` and add `TRANSLATE_LEASE_MS` (180 000) and `TRANSLATE_CANCEL_GRACE_MS` (20 000).\n- **Line 39:** the `TranslateJob` methods gain `read_lease` and `abandon` (a conditional DELETE).\n- **Line 41:** a page job can also end with its row deleted (abandoned).\n- **Store functions:** name `renew_translate_lease`, `cancel_translate_lease` and `claim_translate_job`'s `expired_at` drop.\n- **Line 52:** the in-place migration adds `wanted_at`.\n- **Media fetch:** if the README describes the media fetch as byte-capped, that is false now. Only `fetch_bounded` keeps the 2 MB cap.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"client/README.md\" update=\"yes\">\nThe new gateway route is undocumented. What has to change:\n- **Line 28:** the 401 list names the translate cancel.\n- **New bullet, `POST /api/translate/cancel {id, host}`:**\n  - its own rate-limit bucket (429);\n  - `X-Profile-Key` checked before the body (401);\n  - the same 400 texts as `POST /api/translate`;\n  - one bridge POST to `/internal/translate/cancel` (6 s);\n  - answers `{state, available}`;\n  - an Engine 404 `Video not found` answers `{none, false}`;\n  - any other failure answers 502 `Engine translate failed`.\n- **Line 45:** the bridge-call list gains the cancel.\n- **Lines 51 and 58-59:** the route lists gain `/api/translate/cancel` and `/internal/translate/cancel`.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"client/frontend/README.md\" update=\"yes\">\nRecommendation 1 was not taken: the poll still ends on queued or running without `available`, so the \"requests nothing and polls nothing\" wording stays. What has to change:\n- **Line 8:** the gateway routes gain `POST /api/translate/cancel`.\n- **Line 29:** a state poll that answers `none` with `available` true while Translate is on sends `requestTranslate` again and handles the answer as turnOn does (`applyFetched`). The next `queued` counts as a change, so polling restarts at 2 s. A failed re-request takes the poll's error path: a 401 shows its message, and anything else retries with backoff.\n- **Line 30:** \"Turning Translate off ends the chain and clears the lines\" gains: it also sends one `cancelTranslate` (`POST /api/translate/cancel {id, host}`) once any translate request in flight has settled. It does not wait for the answer, and a failure is ignored.\n- **Line 31:** the claim that `none` ends the poll is now false for `none` with `available`. Only a `none` without `available` ends it.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"CONTEXT.md\" update=\"yes\">\n- **New term, Viewer lease:**\n  - a page-queued job's `wanted_at`, renewed by every state read while the job is queued or running;\n  - it lapses 180 s after the last renewal;\n  - a lapsed queued job is dropped at claim and never started;\n  - a lapsed running job is abandoned at the next chunk-loop wake (about 2 s);\n  - a cancel shortens it to a 20 s grace;\n  - command-line jobs have none and run to the end.\n- **Translate job (line 21):**\n  - The end states gain abandonment: the row is deleted, partial cues are discarded, and the job can be requested again. \"A failed video stays failed\" stays.\n  - Add the CLI exception.\n  - Any duration cap wording goes.\n- **Translate state (line 17):** `none` also follows an abandoned job. The page re-requests on a poll-path `none` with `available`.\n- **Claim (line 22):** a claim can end in an abandon, a conditional delete that a racing renewal wins, after which the job continues.\n- **Source-instance fetch (line 20):** \"caps the bytes it reads\" is false for the media download. JSON and WebVTT keep the 2 MB cap through `fetch_bounded`, and the media stream is bounded by its socket timeout, `stop` and the worker's backpressure.\n- **Generation available (line 18):** no change, because recommendation 1 was not taken.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"DEPLOYMENT.md\" update=\"yes\">\nRecommendation 1 was declined and recommendation 2 has no log line, so the triage notes below are written for that state. What has to change:\n- **Line 98:**\n  - \"Nothing prunes it\" becomes: the worker deletes page jobs whose viewer lease lapsed (queued at claim, running at a wake), and tracks and finished jobs are never pruned.\n  - The writer sentence gains the Engine's lease renewal on queued or running state reads (a failure is logged and the answer is unchanged) and `/internal/translate/cancel` (a store error answers 503, which reaches the page as a 502 that it ignores).\n- **Line 236:** drop the `--max-duration` sentence about the page route skipping the duration check. Add that page jobs carry a viewer lease: a job no one polls for 180 s is dropped, and turning Translate off cancels it after about 20 s.\n- **Upgrade note, near lines 254-263:**\n  - Remove `--max-duration` and `--max-bytes` from any customised `ExecStart` first. Otherwise argparse exits 2 and the unit restart-loops (`RestartPreventExitStatus=6` only).\n  - Then run `sudo systemctl restart peertube-translate-worker`, because `deploy-bluegreen.sh` never restarts the worker.\n  - The Client and the frontend build ship cancel together. An older Engine answers cancel 404, the Client turns that into a 502, and the page ignores it.\n- **Line 270:** the stop also wakes a reader parked on a full lookahead, and a feeder blocked writing ends when ffmpeg is killed.\n- **Lines 279-280:** delete the `--max-duration` and `--max-bytes` rows.\n- **Line 290:** delete `--max-duration` from the enqueue paragraph.\n- **Line 297:** drop `duration Ns over Ms`.\n- **Triage:**\n  - A page job that vanished, with the journal line `abandoned, no viewer`: no viewer polled for 180 s, or Translate was turned off.\n  - \"Jobs stay `queued`\" (row 355): leased page jobs whose lease lapsed are dropped silently at the next claim.\n  - A worker stop or restart longer than 15 s makes `available` false. The page then stops polling, so waiting viewers' jobs lapse, and they must turn Translate off and on.\n- **Lines 586 and 593:** the route lists gain `/api/translate/cancel` and `/internal/translate/cancel`.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"README.md\" update=\"yes\">\n- **Line 53:** the gateway row lists `profile-gated /api/translate`. Add `/api/translate/cancel`, which shortens a job's viewer lease when Translate is turned off.\n- **Line 54:** the internal contract row lists `/internal/translate` and `/internal/translate/enqueue`. Add `/internal/translate/cancel`.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"DATA_BUILD.md\" update=\"yes\">\nLine 15 lists the Engine's writes to `subtitles.db` as caching tracks and inserting queued jobs. Add:\n- its lease renewal on queued or running state reads from `/internal/translate`;\n- its lease cap from `/internal/translate/cancel`;\n- the worker's deletion of page jobs whose lease lapsed.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/roadmap.md\" update=\"yes\">\n- **Line 62:** the F11-M2 PARTIAL Delivered list gains the build's work, with the plan link: duration and media-size caps removed, a bounded decoded-audio lookahead, the viewer lease with abandonment, and cancel on Translate off.\n- **Optional:** a DONE bullet beside lines 24-25 in the same style.\n</doc>\n</docs>\n\n<adr_conflicts>\nnone\n</adr_conflicts>",
    "step_9_i2_update:engine/server/db/jobs/docs/TRANSLATE_WORKER.md": "<changes>\nI updated `TRANSLATE_WORKER.md`: the duration and media-size caps are removed, and the doc now covers the bounded lookahead with backpressure and the viewer lease, cancel and abandonment, including the command-line exception.\n\nI checked each statement against `translate-worker.py` and `subtitles.py` (`AudioPipe`, `lease_lapsed`, `translate_audio`, `run_job`, `serve`, `claim_translate_job`, `read_lease`, `abandon`, `_recover_translate_jobs`, `parse_args`).\n\n- **Purpose:** the pointer to `engine/server/README.md` now says \"the Engine's translate routes\" instead of \"both Engine routes\".\n- **Job Lifecycle:** a `queued` row from the page carries `wanted_at` and a CLI row carries NULL. A new end path, abandonment, deletes the row at claim or at a chunk-loop wake. That leaves no row and no partial cues, so the state reads `none` and the job can be queued again. \"A failed key is never queued again\" is kept.\n- **Enqueue:**\n  - Removed `--max-duration`, the stored-duration check and `refused: duration Ns over Ms`.\n  - The CLI queues with NULL `wanted_at` and runs to the end.\n  - The Engine's enqueue route stamps `wanted_at`. The sentence about the page route skipping the duration check is gone.\n- **Run flags:** only `--max-chunk-seconds` and `--stall-seconds` remain.\n- **Serve Loop:** the claim takes `expired_at = now - TRANSLATE_LEASE_MS` and first deletes lapsed queued leased rows in the same IMMEDIATE transaction. This writes no log line. Each pass runs a job until it ends or is abandoned.\n- **Job Pipeline:**\n  - Step 3 no longer checks duration.\n  - Step 5 drops the \"all PCM in memory, about 115 MB\" statement. In its place: the download is uncapped, and `AudioPipe` holds at most 600 s (`LOOKAHEAD_SECONDS`) plus one window, about 20 MB. Samples are released after each window, and a full buffer stops the reader so ffmpeg and the download wait. It also notes the risk that a send timeout ends the job `media download failed`.\n- **Bounds:** removed the Duration and Media size rows and added Lookahead and Viewer lease rows. The constant column now names where each constant lives.\n- **Chunking:** one clause notes that each whole `cues_json` rewrite grows with the cue count.\n- **New section, Viewer Lease and Cancel:**\n  - when a lease counts as lapsed;\n  - renewal, which points to `engine/server/README.md` for the routes;\n  - the cancel cap to the 20 s grace, which never lengthens a lease;\n  - the drop at claim;\n  - the check at each wake: `lease_lapsed`, then `read_lease` while the claim holds, then `abandon` as one conditional DELETE, then `JobAbandoned`.     "step_9_i2_update:engine/server/README.md": "<changes>\nengine/server/README.md now describes the viewer lease (`wanted_at`), lease renewal on state reads, the `/internal/translate/cancel` route and the new store functions. Before claiming, it deletes queued leased rows whose lease has lapsed.\n  - The `TranslateJob` methods now include `read_lease` and `abandon`. `abandon` is a conditional DELETE, so a renewal that lands first wins.\n  - `enqueue_translate_job` takes a keyword `wanted_at`. Command-line jobs carry none, so they are never renewed, shortened, dropped or abandoned.\n  - New bullet for `renew_translate_lease` and `cancel_translate_lease`.\n  - The end states now include a page job that is deleted when its lease lapses. Afterwards its state reads `none`.\n- **Left as is:**\n  - The Notes migration sentence (\"adds whatever is missing of the job columns\") already covers `wanted_at`.\n  - The README never said the media fetch had a byte cap, so there was nothing to fix there.\n\nI checked every statement against `internal_translate.py`, `subtitles.py`, `server_config.py`, `router.py` and `translate-worker.py`.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:client/README.md": "<changes>\nI documented the `POST /api/translate/cancel` gateway route in `client/README.md` and added it, plus the Engine's `/internal/translate/cancel`, to the 401 list, the bridge-call list and the boundary lists.\n\nI checked each statement against `client/backend/server.py` (around lines 561\u2013571 and 1137) and `client/backend/lib/engine_api_client.py` (`_post_translate` and `cancel_translate`, lines 222\u2013242).\n\n- **The 401 list:** it now includes \"translate cancel\".\n- **New bullet after `POST /api/translate`:**\n  - The route shortens one video's viewer lease to the cancel grace, for a profile holder. The page sends it when Translate is turned off.\n  - Its checks run in the same order and give the same 400 texts as `POST /api/translate`, but it has its own rate-limit bucket (429 `Rate limit exceeded`).\n  - It sends one bridge POST to `/internal/translate/cancel` with a 6 s timeout.\n  - It answers `{state, available}` with no cues. `state` is the job's stored state after the cancel, or `none` if there is no row, and is never `busy`.\n  - An Engine 404 `Video not found` answers `{none, false}`.     "step_9_i2_update:client/frontend/README.md": "<changes>\nI updated `client/frontend/README.md` so the video page covers both new Translate behaviours: it sends a cancel when Translate is turned off, and it requests the translation again when a poll reads `none` while generation is available.     "step_9_i2_update:CONTEXT.md": "<changes>\nI added a **Viewer lease** term to CONTEXT.md and updated Translate state, Translate job, Claim and Source-instance fetch to match.\n\n- **Viewer lease (new term, after Claim):**\n  - It is a page-queued job's `wanted_at`. The Engine sets it at enqueue, and every state read renews it while the job is `queued` or `running`.\n  - It lapses 180 s (`TRANSLATE_LEASE_MS`) after the last renewal. A lapsed queued job is dropped at claim. A lapsed running job is abandoned at the next chunk-loop wake (about 2 s).\n  - A cancel from turning Translate off shortens the lease to a 20 s grace (`TRANSLATE_CANCEL_GRACE_MS`) and never lengthens it, so a job another viewer is still polling survives.\n  - Command-line jobs have no lease (NULL) and are never renewed, shortened, dropped or abandoned.\n  - It points to `TRANSLATE_WORKER.md` for the worker's side.\n- **Translate state:** `none` also follows an abandoned job. A page still on Translate that polls `none` with `available` requests generation again.\n- **Translate job:**\n  - \"Abandoned\" is now a fourth end: the row is deleted with its partial cues, the state reads `none`, and the video can be requested again. \"A `failed` video stays failed\" is kept.\n  - Command-line jobs carry no lease and run to the end.\n  - The entry had no duration-cap wording to remove.\n- **Claim:** an abandon is the one claim write that deletes. It removes the row only while the claim holds and the lease is still lapsed, so a renewal that lands first wins and the job continues.\n- **Source-instance fetch:** \"caps the bytes it reads\" now applies only to JSON and WebVTT bodies. The media download is uncapped, bounded by its socket timeout and the worker's backpressure.\n\nI checked these against the code: `server_config.py` (the 180 000 and 20 000 constants), `POLL_SECONDS = 2.0` and `lease_lapsed` in the worker, the \"uncapped, under a socket timeout only\" wording in `source_fetch.py`'s module docstring, and `applyFetched` and `cancelTranslate` in `translate.ts`. The Generation available entry is unchanged.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:DEPLOYMENT.md": "<changes>\nI updated DEPLOYMENT.md: the duration and media-size caps are gone from it, and it now covers the viewer lease, cancel, abandonment and the worker upgrade steps.\n\n- **`subtitles.db` paragraph (section 1):**\n  - \"Nothing prunes it\" is replaced.   "requirements": "### Purpose\nAny whitelisted video can be translated, whatever its length. The single GPU translate worker spends time only on videos that a viewer is still waiting for. The duration cap and the media-size cap go, because the media is streamed and never stored. What the caps were standing in for is handled directly:\n- bounded memory;\n- a viewer lease, so a viewer who gives up (closes the video or the tab, or turns Translate off) does not leave the worker busy;\n- an explicit cancel.\n\n### Background (operator's debug session, 2026-10-09, re-checked in the tree)\n- Translation was \"not working\" because of the caps. Since the last success on 10-06, 7 jobs failed with `duration Ns over 3600s`, including both of the operator's attempts that day (7754 s and 5284 s). The other failures came from the videos themselves: music with no speech, an HTTP 403, an incomplete cert chain, and one transient CUDA OOM. A 295 s control video ended `ready`.\n- The 7 cap-failed rows were deleted on 2026-10-09 by `.scratch/translate-debug/clear_cap_failures.py`. The build carries no cleanup.\n- In `engine/server/db/jobs/translate-worker.py`:\n  - `AudioPipe` streams the download into ffmpeg's stdin through `stream_media` and never writes it to disk.\n  - `_read` (line ~218) appends every decoded sample to `self.pcm` and never drops any (rat-tail at line 182). The only bound on that buffer is `max_samples` (line 227, `audio longer than Ns`), and it grows by about 115 MB per hour of audio.\n  - `_read` drains ffmpeg as fast as the network allows. The Engine and the worker both use `now_ms()` on the same host.\n- **Renewal.**\n  - When the state route reads a `queued` or `running` row, it sets `wanted_at = now` in the same `subtitles_db_lock` hold. a `keepalive` fetch on `pagehide` is a possible later addition);\n  - any cleanup of the cap-failed rows (already done by the operator).\n\n### Documentation to update\n- **`TRANSLATE_WORKER.md`:**\n  - Bounds; Media File Choice; Job Pipeline;\n  - Error Texts: remove `duration Ns over Ms`, `audio longer than Ns`, `video duration unknown` and `media over N bytes`;\n  - the in-memory PCM statement, which becomes a bounded lookahead with backpressure;\n  - the CLI flags;\n  - a new section on the viewer lease, cancel and abandonment, including the CLI exception.\n- **`engine/server/README.md`:** the `wanted_at` column, the new store functions, renewal on the state route, and the cancel route. The tunables list drops the two caps and adds the lease and grace constants.\n- **`client/README.md`:** the `POST /api/translate/cancel` gateway route.\n- **`CONTEXT.md`:**\n  - Translate job: the lease, abandonment, the CLI exception;\n  - Translate state: `none` after abandonment;\n  - a new term, **Viewer lease**.\n- **`DEPLOYMENT.md`:**\n  - line 236: drop the sentence about the page route skipping the duration check, and mention the lease;\n  - lines 279-280: drop the `--max-duration` and `--max-bytes` rows from the `run` flags table;\n  - line 290: drop `--max-duration` from the `enqueue` paragraph;\n  - add `/internal/translate/cancel` to the boundary contract list.\n\n### Risks, tradeoffs and named simplifications\n- **R1 Background-tab throttling.** Chrome limits chained timers in a tab hidden for more than 5 minutes to about once a minute. That is why the lease is 180 s. If it lapses anyway, the AC6 re-request restarts the job from zero.\n- **R2 Remote send timeouts under backpressure.** While the lookahead is full, the socket is read only as Whisper frees space. A hung Whisper call can let a server's send timeout (nginx's default is 60 s) reset the connection, and the job then fails `media download failed`. The existing 600 s stall detector already marks a hung worker unavailable.\n- **R3 Unleased CLI jobs have no bound.** A CLI-queued endless stream runs until stopped. This is accepted, because the operator issues CLI jobs.\n- **R4 A write on every poll.** Each poll on a queued or running job is one short UPDATE every 2\u201316 s per waiting viewer, in WAL mode, with a 30 s busy timeout. A failed renewal is logged and not surfaced.\n- **R5 Blue/green.** An older Engine without renewal serves polls only during the 30 s switch drain, which is well under the 180 s lease. An older worker ignores `wanted_at` and runs jobs to the end, which is today's behaviour.\n- **R6 A long job blocks the queue.** One job runs at a time, so a 3-hour video holds the GPU for about 10 minutes. Upgrade path: append-only cue storage.\n- **Tradeoffs accepted:**\n  - An abandoned job loses its work.\n  - A cancel takes effect after about 20 s.\n  - A lapsed hidden tab restarts the job.\n  - A very long video is not refused up front. It is simply slow, and only while someone waits.\n\n### Conflicts already resolved by the operator\n- **AC6 against \"a key is never re-queued\".** That rule applies to `failed` rows. It deletes the bytes before `upto` from the front of `pcm`, advances `base` and calls `notify_all`. `translate_audio` calls it right after `pos += cut`.\n- `AudioPipe` takes the window length (`max_chunk` samples) and computes `limit = LOOKAHEAD_SECONDS * SAMPLE_RATE + max_chunk`. `LOOKAHEAD_SECONDS = 600` is a new worker constant.\n- Before each read, `_read` waits on the condition until the room (`limit` minus the samples buffered) is positive, or until `stop` is set or an error is recorded. It then calls `read1(min(READ_CHUNK_BYTES, room in bytes))`.\n  - Clamping the read size means the buffer never exceeds the limit, not even by one read chunk. CLI jobs are never renewed, shortened, dropped at claim or abandoned.\n- `requeue` (`JobStopped`, `WhitelistBusy`) and `_recover_translate_jobs` do not touch `wanted_at`, so a lease survives a requeue unchanged.\n\n**Contract fixture and tests.**\n- **Fixture:** `translate_contract.json` gains `cancel` route cases. They cover every stored state with and without `available`, the 404 `Video not found` mapping to `{none, false}`, the missing-route 404 rejected, `busy` rejected, an unknown state rejected, and `available` as a string rejected. The description text names the third route. The three replaying tests (`test_engine_api_client.py`, `test_frontend_translate.py`, `test_internal_translate.py`) learn the route.\n- **Worker tests:**\n  - A no-duration JSON and a long stored duration both translate.\n  - `AudioPipe`'s logical length never exceeds `limit` against a fake ffmpeg producing more than the limit, and `_read` parks and resumes on `release`. A `--max-chunk-seconds` above `LOOKAHEAD` does not deadlock, and `close` wakes a parked reader.\n  - An expired lease abandons the job, deletes the row and logs one line.\n  - A renewal between the read and the delete keeps the job.\n  - A CLI job is never abandoned.\n- **Store tests:**\n  - The claim drops expired leased queued rows but keeps unleased and fresh ones.\n  - Renewal and cancel touch only leased queued and running rows, and cancel never lengthens a lease.\n  - Migration adds `wanted_at` in place.\n- **Route tests:** the Engine route covers 400, 404, 503, closed store, and renewal on read. The Client route covers 401 before the body, 400, 429 and 502.\n- **Frontend tests:** cancel on `turnOff`, cancel ordered after an in-flight poll, and re-request on poll-path `none` with `available`.\n\n**Docs.** `TRANSLATE_WORKER.md`, `engine/server/README.md`, `client/README.md`, `CONTEXT.md` (a new **Viewer lease** term) and `DEPLOYMENT.md` are updated as listed in the requirements.\n\n### Alternatives considered\n\n- **A separate lease table or per-viewer rows.** Rejected: per-viewer accounting is out of scope. A single column with renewal piggybacked on the existing poll needs no new request, and its write is gated to `queued` and `running` rows.\n- **The Engine signalling the worker directly (signal or socket).** Rejected: the Engine and the worker share only `subtitles.db`. The worker already wakes every 2 s, so a database read is enough.\n- **Spooling PCM to a temp file to bound memory.** Rejected: the purpose is that media is never stored, and backpressure needs no disk.\n- **A deque of chunks instead of a `bytearray` with `base`.** Rejected: `slice` would have to join across chunks. Trimming the front of one buffer keeps `slice` a single contiguous copy.\n- **Pulling ffmpeg output from the main thread on demand, with no reader thread.** Rejected: it would lose the 2 s wake that the stop and lease checks need, and it reintroduces pipe-deadlock risk with stderr.\n- **Throttling the lease read to every N seconds.** Rejected: one primary-key read per chunk is cheaper than the per-chunk cue rewrite, and a throttle would only add state.\n- **Abandon with a plain DELETE after the read.** Rejected for the settled conditional DELETE, so a renewal that races the check wins.\n- **On a lost abandon race, fail the job or leave it running.** I chose to requeue: a viewer came back, and requeuing keeps the claim count honest.\n- **Cancelling in-flight requests with `AbortController` on turnOff.** Rejected: aborting the browser fetch does not stop a request the gateway has already forwarded. Ordering the cancel after the in-flight request settles is what actually removes the race.\n- **Guarding the AC6 re-request on the previous state being `queued` or `running`.** Rejected: it narrows AC6's wording. Using the backoff delay keeps AC6 literal and still prevents a spin.\n- **`DELETE /api/translate`.** The operator chose `POST /api/translate/cancel` (decision of 2026-10-09).\n\n### Gotchas, risks and limitations\n\n- **Expired queued rows count against `SUBTITLE_QUEUE_CAP` until the next claim.** While one long job runs, cancelled or lapsed queued rows can hold cap slots, so a new viewer may see `busy`. With a cap of 50 this is unlikely. Upgrade path: the same expired-row DELETE in `enqueue_translate_job`.\n- **Enqueue does not renew an existing row.** A viewer whose enqueue answers `exists` for a lapsed queued row renews it only at the first poll, 2 s later. If the worker drops the row in that window, the poll reads `none` and AC6 re-requests it. This heals itself, at the cost of one extra round trip.\n- **Bytearray allocation.** Front deletion of a `bytearray` trims the logical length at once, but CPython may keep up to about twice that allocated until it compacts. The test asserts the logical length (the AC3 bound), not the RSS.\n- **Shutdown under backpressure.** `close` must notify the condition after setting `stop`, and `_read` must still reap ffmpeg after an early exit. Otherwise shutdown hangs on a parked reader. The tests pin both.\n- **Remote send timeouts (R2).** These are made more likely by backpressure, and a hung Whisper call can turn into `media download failed`. Accepted as R2.\n- **One viewer's cancel affects co-viewers.** It shortens the lease for everyone. A co-viewer in a hidden tab polling once a minute (R1) then loses the job after 20 s, and their AC6 re-request restarts it from zero.\n- **A CLI enqueue of a key that already has a leased viewer job answers `already present`.** The job stays leased and can still be abandoned. Converting a viewer job to a CLI job is not provided.\n- **Lease arithmetic uses `now_ms()` on one host for the Engine and the worker.** A clock step backwards lengthens leases, and a step forwards can abandon a job early. AC6 re-requests in that case.\n- **An instance-track takeover leaves stale `wanted_at` on a ready row.** It is inert, because every lease statement is state-gated.\n\n### Tradeoffs the operator is asked to accept\n\n- An abandoned job loses all its work, and a re-request starts from zero.\n- A cancel takes effect after about 20 s plus one chunk, not at once.\n- A hidden tab whose timers lapse past 180 s restarts its job.\n- One viewer's cancel can cost a slow-polling co-viewer a restart.\n- A very long video is never refused. It holds the single GPU for its whole run while someone waits, and an unleased CLI job holds it until it ends.\n- Every poll on a queued or running job is one short write.\n- The whole-list running-cue rewrite stays O(cues) per chunk. This is the named simplification: its ceiling is very long videos, and its upgrade path is append-only cue storage.\n- **Two refinements of the settled design that I am choosing and naming:**\n  - The cancel is ordered after the page's in-flight request. This narrows the named turn-off race; it does not widen anything.\n  - A poll-path re-request follows up with the backoff delay, not 0.\n- **A deliberate choice to confirm:** when the abandon DELETE loses to a renewal, the job is requeued, not continued.
